newsitem.title: BRAZIL: At least 12 dead in Amazon riverboat disaster.
newsitem.headline: At least 12 dead in Amazon riverboat disaster.

text.p: At least 12 people died and 20 were missing on Saturday when a riverboat with more than 80 people onboard sank in a remote region of the Amazon, a port official said.

Lieutenant Paulo de Olivera, of the Belem Port Authority, said the riverboat sank in the middle of the night while it was heading toward the small town of Acara, 120 miles (190 km) down river from Belem city.
"We don't know what happened and we don't know the exact number of dead. The boat probably hit a log and went under," Olivera said in a telephone interview.
He said the Belem Port Authority had sent a launch with divers to help in the rescue operations but that the exact number of dead would not be known until the launch returned.
"The site of the accident is very remote and difficult to reach," said Olivera.
Acara, a small town founded next to a river which carries the same name, only has one phone which was out of service on Saturday.
Riverboats are the preferred method of transport in the Amazon where the population takes advantage of a vast river network to move from one town to another.
